# Whale Waker

**Scheduled wake-ups for the residents of a workspace.**
Each target — a "whale" — gets its own inte

rval, quiet hours, daily cap, prompt and
deny-list. Every wake-up reuses the same session, gathers w

hat changed since last
time, and sends one short prompt.

- Package: `dsh-whale-waker`
- Version: **0.4.1**
- License: MIT
- Author: Bao · E-1021

> Why: an agent that only exists while you type is a tool. An agent that wakes on
> its own, reads w

hat changed, and decides to do one small thing — that is closer
> to a resident. This plugin is the

d decides to do one small thing — that is closer
> to a resident. This plugin is the clock for that.
## Install

From a local checkout:

Or install the directory through `plugin_manager`'s `install_bundle` in the app.
Restart DSH afterwa
rds — plugin modules are cached by URL.
The settings page shows up in **Settings → Whale Waker** right after that.
## Configure
Settings live in `dsh-whale-waker.json`:

- `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR/dsh-whale-waker.json` by default,
- or `config.configPath` from the row config.

The page edits the file for you; the scheduler re-reads it when the mtime changes
(checked every fiv

its the file for you; the scheduler re-reads it when the mtime changes
(checked every five minutes).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Meaning |

| `id` | Target name; also the session id (`walk-<id>`) and the log tag. |
| `workspace` | The room
this whale lives in. Files changed here become material. **Required**: empty means no wake-up happen

s (`no-workspace`). |
| `provider` / `model` | Optional. Empty means "use this DSH's default model",
so the plugin does not assume a vendor. A provider this host does not serve is logged and skipped a

s `provider-not-configured` instead of failing inside agent creation. |
| `ollamaBase` | Endpoint us
ed only to pre-warm an `ollama*` provider. Default `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, 15 s timeout, and a fai

lure never blocks the wake-up. |
| `intervalMinutes` | How often it may wake on its own (5–2880). |

| `minGapMinutes` | Minimum gap between two wake-ups (0–1440). |
| `startHour` / `endHour` | Quiet h

ours: outside this window nothing fires (0–24). |
| `maxPerDay` | Hard daily cap (0–48). `0` means n

ever wake on its own. |
| `dryRun` | Collect material and log it, but do not open a session. |
| `wa

tch` | Extra directories whose fresh files are listed as material. |
| `stateSection` | Heading in `

STATE.md` whose bullets are quoted (default `## In progress`). |
| `denyTools` | Tool names removed

from that whale's wake session (e.g. another agent's private tools). |
| `activeWindowMinutes` | Aft
er a human actually talks in that workspace, the timer stays quiet this long (default 10; `0` disabl

es). Manual wake-ups ignore it. |
| `prompt` | Template; `{material}` is replaced. |
| `name` | Disp

lay name used in the session title (defaults to `id`). |
| `sessionTitle` | Title template for the w
ake session; `{name}` is replaced (default `Wake · {name}`). |

State (last wake, today's count) is persisted to `dsh-whale-waker-state.json` next to
the config, so
restarting DSH does not re-fire everybody.
## Language

The settings page follows the DSH locale by default, and can be switched per
plugin without touching
the rest of the UI:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Supported values: `auto` (follow DSH), `en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`. The selector sits
near the top of the
page; the choice is written to the same config file.
## While you are talking to it

A wake-up never joins your live chat: it opens (or resumes) its own session,
`walk-<id>`, in that wo

rkspace. So the honest answer to "would it start walking
while I am mid-conversation?" is **yes, unl
ess something stops it**.

So something stops it. The plugin watches `agent/inbox/claimed` for messages a
human actually typed

(its own injected prompts and `walk-*` sessions are ignored).
If the workspace saw one within `activ

eWindowMinutes` (default 10), the timer wake
is skipped and logged as `user-active`. The next tick,

five minutes later, tries
again.
What this does **not** do:

- It does not interrupt a wake-up already running.
- It does not persist: after a restart the activi

ty map is empty until the next
message. `minGapMinutes` is the backstop for that window.
- It does n

ot block manual wake-ups (`wake_whale`, or the page's "Wake once") —
those are explicit intent and p

ual wake-ups (`wake_whale`, or the page's "Wake once") —
those are explicit intent and pass `force`.
## Workspace path

The address under each target is editable: type a folder and press **Apply**.
The host validates it

(absolute, existing, a directory), stores the canonical
spelling, and — when no workspace owns that

folder — creates one titled after the
[该节后续省略]
## What a wake-up does

1. Collects material: files changed in the workspace since the last wake, plus
`watch` directories,

plus the `stateSection` bullets of `STATE.md`.
2. Mounts an agent preset so the session has real too

ls (without one, a wake session
cannot even read its own `STATE.md`).
3. Reuses `walk-<id>-<workspac

e fingerprint>` — created the first time, resumed
afterwards. The fingerprint changes with the works

pace path, so a moved room
gets a fresh session instead of resuming one that still points at the old

path.
4. Attaches that session to the workspace group that matches its cwd.
5. Sends the prompt and

waits for the turn to actually end (claim → `turn/end`).
The session stays alive afterwards, so the

conversation remains visible in
that workspace.
6. Names the session from `sessionTitle` (default `

Wake · {name}`), because the
automatic titler ignores prompts that a plugin injects and would otherw

ise
leave it "Untitled" in the sidebar.

Everything is logged to `dsh-whale-waker.log` next to the config, including the material
that was ha
nded over — so "why did it say that" is answerable afterwards.
